purpose: Bounded world-server trace introduced by #188 and source-reviewed on 2026-09-05 at 7eaf8ddc (production code 93e4002a): map/creature loops, supporting periodic tasks and the diagnostic Session creature path. Not an exhaustive inventory of all process timers or proof of production phase conformance. The unspawned world_update timing helper is documented separately, not counted as a clock.
validation_contract: every clock names an existing source file; identifier-shaped entries must name a function defined there, while descriptive entries are not resolved
every clock states its cadence source, its diff source and whether it is production or diagnostic
delivers_under_map_guard must be false; this checks the declaration, not function-body lock, await or delivery behavior
each clock declares a nonempty resolution guard; the checker does not prove that mechanism executes or prevents duplicate transitions
each supplied regression anchor names an existing test function; empty lists are accepted and this check does not execute tests
spawn reachability, exact cadence/phase semantics, invariant coverage and current runtime acceptance require source review and affected integration evidence

clocks.diff_source: measured elapsed wall clock, clamped to u32, zero-diff ticks skipped
owns: the world phase of every ready session, before the map tick is admitted (#787)
the split tick's map-phase session requests and their completion boundary (#787)
the creature frame of every admitted map: lifecycle, movement, aggro and threat, spell and melee on the canonical incarnations (#1263 F6-8D3b-1; the only creature runtime since F6-8E-1)
clocks.delivery_note: recipients and packets are collected inside the guarded block and delivered after the map lock is released; the #787 split releases every synchronous guard — respawn mutation order, MapManager and spawn metadata — before any phase request is delivered or any completion awaited, and re-takes them only to resume the same tick with the diff saved at the split. Each step issues the world phase first (World.cpp:2704) and admits the map tick only after it is quiescent (World.cpp:2748); a claimed pass whose end cannot be observed abandons the tick instead of resuming over it.
clocks.resolution_guard: World disconnect completion includes task-owned finalization and active registration retirement. Unresolved permits, including InterruptedAfterStart, hold the barrier across producer steps. Shutdown pauses ordinary simulation while session tasks drain; the final respawn tick requires an empty active-session registry. The admitted creature executor runs each creature phase once per admitted tick under the creature execution lease (#1263 F6-8D2/D3b); no other creature runtime exists (F6-8E-1 deleted the legacy loop, the session creature tick and the tick owner).

tick_owner.constructed_default: none: the canonical map update loop is the only creature runtime
tick_owner.production_default_mechanism: app startup spawns only the canonical map loop; the retired keys RustyCore.LegacyCreatureGlobalRuntime and RustyCore.CanonicalCreatureRuntime are only warned (crates/world-server/src/bootstrap/config.rs::warn_retired_creature_tick_owner_keys_like_cpp)
tick_owner.note: There is no owner to select: the legacy global creature loop, the per-session creature tick and the owner value were deleted together. This is source configuration evidence, not a runtime acceptance result.
